c.tagline: Harbour city of sails, volcanoes and endless coastline.

taxi.fareNote: Metered fares vary by company; agree on a fixed price for airport transfers or use SkyBus/rideshare instead.

emergency.note: 111 is the single emergency number for police, fire and ambulance nationwide; Auckland City Hospital operates the main public emergency department.

english.label: Easy to get by in English

avoid.reason: Watch for late-night rowdiness on lower Queen Street and Karangahape Road, and never leave valuables in parked cars at beaches or trailheads.

hood_desc: The commercial and entertainment core with Sky Tower, Queen Street shopping, waterfront ferries, and Britomart's dining precinct; suits first-timers who want everything walkable and no transport hassle.
Waterfront marina district with superyachts, upscale seafood restaurants, and easy walk to Sky Tower and the Ferry Building; suits couples and business travelers wanting a scenic, polished base.
Auckland's trendiest strip of villas, boutiques, cafes and bars along Ponsonby Road; suits foodies, younger travelers and anyone wanting a distinct neighborhood vibe just outside the CBD.
Leafy, historic garden suburb with boutique shops, Auckland Domain and the Museum nearby; suits couples and travelers wanting a quieter, upscale base a short bus or walk from downtown.
A charming harbourside village reached by a scenic 12-minute ferry ride, with beaches, cafes and Victorian villas; suits travelers wanting a relaxed, low-key stay with easy CBD access by boat.
lodging: Ascot Parnell Boutique Bed and Breakfast

water.note: Tap water is treated to high standards and safe to drink straight from the tap.

sys.n: Auckland Metro (electric train network: Southern, Western, Eastern, Onehunga lines)
AT Metro Bus (including City Link, Inner Link, Outer Link)
Auckland Ferry (to Devonport, Waiheke Island, Half Moon Bay etc.)
Northern Busway (dedicated bus rapid transit corridor)

transit.pay: Visitors tap on/off with an AT HOP card (available from stations, retailers or the AT Metro app) loaded with cash; contactless bank card and Apple/Google Pay tap-and-go is also accepted on trains, most buses and ferries. Single paper tickets are not available on trains.
transit.hours: Trains and buses run roughly 5am-midnight on weekdays with reduced late-night and Sunday frequency; there is no true 24-hour service, so night owls rely on taxis or rideshare after midnight.
transit.note: The City Rail Link (a new underground rail tunnel through downtown) has been under construction and is progressively opening, improving cross-city train frequency.

train: Auckland Metro suburban rail (Southern, Western, Eastern, Onehunga lines)
Northern Explorer long-distance train to Wellington
bus: AT Metro city and regional buses
ferry: Fullers360 ferries to Devonport, Waiheke Island, Rangitoto and other Hauraki Gulf destinations

transit.m: SkyBus Airport Express (bus, ~45-60 min to CBD)

tip.r: Tipping is not customary in New Zealand; a small tip for exceptional service is appreciated but never expected, and service charges are rarely added.
